solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Vendors rejected broadcast work by this writer

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the run of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: to broadcast is to air
OP is short for opus, a work
the setter refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: Traders turn down a radio piece the writer has produced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vendors' here means places that sell, i.e. shops and markets, not the people selling.
explanation.definitionFit: Large shops or trading centres are places that sell goods, so they serve as vendors.

clue.text: Girl upset about Greek character and chaplain, ineffectual men

indicators.note: about says the first piece goes round the others
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: Sue is a girl's name
nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
CH abbreviates chaplain

explanation.surface: A girl annoyed with a Greek and a padre thinks men useless.
explanation.definitionFit: Castrated men are figuratively powerless, ineffectual.

clue.text: Chap to become exhausted, missing out

indicators.note: missing says the next word is removed

parts.note: to peter out is to become exhausted

explanation.surface: A man running out of steam and left out.
explanation.definitionFit: A common man's name, and a chap is any man.

clue.text: Upset a pilot and member of ground crew?

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the word upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: per means a, as in so much a head
a pilot is an airman

explanation.surface: An unsettled pilot and someone from the airfield staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' is per, as in 'ten pounds a head'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground crew mend aircraft, so a mender of things belongs there.

clue.text: Jelly, when still?

parts.note: as means when, as in as I left
a still is a photograph, a pic

explanation.surface: Asking whether a jelly is set when it stops wobbling.
explanation.definitionFit: A savoury gelatine made from meat stock is a jelly.

clue.text: Passing first of cases of white wine

parts.note: a passing is a death, a demise

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Someone dies, and the first thing from the crates is opened: some white wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A medium-dry style of sparkling wine, usually Champagne, which is generally white.

clue.text: European city investing nothing in doctors, really

indicators.note: investing means putting into, so the letter goes inside
in places the letter inside the doctors

parts.note: DR abbreviates doctor, twice for doctors
O is zero, nothing
echt means genuine, real

explanation.surface: A city that really puts nothing into its doctors.
explanation.walkthrough: ECHT is German for genuine, used in English too.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dutch city in the province of South Holland is in Europe.

clue.text: Saw base, not head, rising

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means read upwards, backwards
not head drops the first letter

parts.note: the bottom is the base

explanation.surface: A saw blade with no top edge, rising off its base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' is the noun for a saying, not a tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or maxim.

clue.text: Calm, with no end of peace and quiet arranged, one's assumed

indicators.note: arranged means put in order, so the letters are rearranged
with no says a letter is taken out

parts.note: sober means calm, staid

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter

explanation.surface: Peace and quiet bring calm in which one settles in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' takes E (the 'end of peace') from SOBER; SOBR and QUIET are then 'arranged'.
explanation.definitionFit: A nickname is a name taken on, one that is assumed.

clue.text: Brass item, with nothing inserted, appearing as gold item?

indicators.note: inserted says the letter goes inside

parts.note: a cornet is a brass instrument
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A brass instrument with nothing in it passing itself off as gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A small crown, often made of gold, is a gold item.

clue.text: Writing material for offline exam?

parts.note: offline means not electronic: NOT E, as in not e-anything
an exam is a paper

explanation.surface: A question about what to write on when the test is done on paper rather than a screen.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'offline exam' as NOT E-PAPER: an exam that is not an electronic paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheets of stationery used for letters are writing material.

clue.text: River relocated by clan — this river?

indicators.note: relocated means moved to a new place, so one letter of the word shifts position

parts.note: a clan is a tribe

explanation.surface: A river moved by a clan: could this be it?
explanation.walkthrough: 'relocated' shifts the R of TRIBE to the end; '— this river?' points back to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The waterway that flows through Rome is a well-known Italian river.

clue.text: Functionary around Queen may be chased by one!

definitions.text: Functionary around Queen may be chased by one!

indicators.note: being chased by something puts that thing after it
around says the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: a functionary is a cog in the machine
R is Regina, the Queen
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A royal attendant might find itself pursued by one of the palace dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: Whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the late Queen's corgis were known to chase, even bite, palace staff.
explanation.definitionFit: The Welsh dog breed famously kept by Queen Elizabeth II might chase a courtier.

clue.text: Is gold set back in crown almost wearing away?

indicators.note: in places the turned pieces inside the trimmed word
almost drops the last letter

parts.note: a corona is a crown

indicators.note: set back means read backwards

parts.note: OR is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A question about whether gold mounted in a crown is nearly worn down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set back' turns IS OR into ROSI, which goes 'in' CORON (CORONA, 'almost').
explanation.definitionFit: Gradual destruction of metal by chemical action is a wearing away.

clue.text: Resort's second gamble not entirely irregular

parts.note: a spa is a resort; the 's gives the S
a mo is a moment, a second

indicators.note: not entirely drops the final letter

parts.note: to dice is to gamble

explanation.surface: A spa town's second flutter is only partly erratic.
explanation.definitionFit: Something occurring in fits and starts is irregular.

clue.text: It doesn't take any pluck to play this

definitions.text: It doesn't take any pluck to play this

parts.words: It doesn't take any pluck to play this
parts.note: pluck means courage and also plucking strings; this mimed instrument has no strings to pluck

explanation.surface: Playing this requires no bravery.
explanation.definitionFit: Miming a rock guitar solo with no instrument involves no actual plucking of strings.

clue.text: Instructions for taking off?

parts.note: taking off suggests aircraft departure but means taking off weight

explanation.surface: Guidance for a pilot before take-off.
explanation.definitionFit: A printed plan for slimming tells a dieter how to shed pounds.

clue.text: Party reforming but displaying lack of faith

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: reforming means putting into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A political party reorganising but showing it has lost belief.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncertainty about what to believe is a lack of faith.

clue.text: Like great speaker of French, excellent about origins of Gallic opinion

parts.note: de is French for of

indicators.note: about says the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: magic means excellent, as in 'that's magic'

indicators.note: origins of picks the first letter of each word

explanation.surface: A grand orator talking French, admirably round a Gallic opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: A demagogue is a powerful speaker, playing on the crowd's prejudices.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabble-rousing orator is a persuasive speaker, so this adjective means like one.

clue.text: Held back some manure ready for second attempt?

indicators.note: Held back says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Dung kept back, ready for another go at the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition included 'for', which is only the link: a repeat is a second attempt, not 'for second attempt'.
explanation.definitionFit: A repeat performance or race run again is a second attempt.

clue.text: Senior soldier in dress cut up cheese

indicators.note: in says the officer goes inside
up in a down clue means read upwards, backwards
cut drops the last letter

parts.note: attire is dress
CO is a commanding officer

explanation.surface: An officer in a ripped uniform tears into some cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft white Italian whey cheese.

clue.text: Redesign of Times a high point, one hazards?

indicators.note: a redesign reworks something, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, a high point

explanation.surface: A newspaper's makeover reaches a peak, and someone takes a chance on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one hazards' means someone who hazards a guess.
explanation.definitionFit: A person making a rough judgement of an amount is hazarding a guess.

clue.text: An opening for collaboration in capital story

indicators.note: in places the pieces inside the capital

parts.note: Rome is the Italian capital

indicators.note: opening for picks the first letter

explanation.surface: A chance to work together on a story in the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: A love story or chivalric tale is a kind of story.

clue.text: She's seduced no curates?

indicators.note: seduced means led astray, so the letters go astray and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A query about a woman of easy virtue who has left the clergy alone.
explanation.walkthrough: Whole clue is both wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A mistress to wealthy men of the court might well tempt churchmen, so it is a fair query.

clue.text: Discrimination some represent as terror-related

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Prejudice leads some to portray a group as linked to terrorism.
explanation.definitionFit: Discernment in aesthetic matters, the ability to tell good from bad, is discrimination.

clue.text: The old penniless writer, upset about daughter lacking funds

indicators.note: about says the reversed pieces go round the next
upset in a down clue turns the pieces upside down, reading backwards

parts.note: ye is an old form of the

indicators.note: penniless says P, for penny, is taken out

parts.note: a pen is a writer

explanation.surface: An old, broke author, upset over his daughter, is short of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penniless' takes P (penny) from PEN; YEEN is 'upset' to NEEY and goes 'about' D.
explanation.definitionFit: Being poor is a state of lacking funds.

clue.text: Tidy place to eat, free of noise, I note

indicators.note: free of says the following pieces are removed

parts.note: a dining room is a place to eat
a din is a noise

explanation.surface: Clean up the restaurant, with no racket, I note.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing DIN, I and N from DINING ROOM leaves G and ROOM.
explanation.definitionFit: To spruce up one's appearance or a horse's coat is to tidy it.

clue.text: Finished on time for everyone to see

parts.note: over means finished

explanation.surface: Done on time, in full view.
explanation.definitionFit: Something open and public is there for all to witness.

clue.text: Groan, say, that finally is swallowed in rejection of courtship

indicators.note: being swallowed in something means going inside it
rejection means turning back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a suit is a courtship, as in paying suit to someone

indicators.note: finally picks the final letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A moan as a romantic approach is turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: Titus Groan is the hero of Mervyn Peake's Gormenghast novels; 'say' marks Groan as one example of a person so named.
explanation.definitionFit: Peake's Titus Groan carries this first name, so a Groan is an example.

clue.text: Woman's right, envying one retaining their looks?

parts.note: Eve is the first woman
envying is being green with envy

explanation.surface: A woman jealous of someone who has kept their good looks.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: a plant that keeps its leaves all year keeps its looks.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant keeping its foliage through winter, or a performer who stays popular, keeps their looks.

clue.text: I'll probe constellation by end of night, having greatest access to sky?

indicators.note: will probe says the letter pushes into the word that follows

parts.note: Aries, the Ram, is a constellation

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter

explanation.surface: An astronomer vows to examine a star group at the end of the night for the best view.
explanation.definitionFit: The most open to the air and breezes, so with the best access to the sky.

clue.text: Sailor recalled island hospital with obligation

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a cay is a small low island
H is the map abbreviation for hospital
a tie is an obligation

explanation.surface: A seaman remembered an island clinic he was bound to.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal term for a yachtsman or yachtswoman, a sailor.
